restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages 0^32 || x and 0^32 || y (x != y, 256-bit little-endian integers): one chunk of one block, chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 (CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT), 5 rounds, unkeyed, the complete 256-bit digest (blake3-r5-prefix-v1). They are found as a collision g(x) = g(y) of the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q, f(x) = digest(0^32 || x), q = 0 here (the digest planes are stored upright); g(x) = g(y) iff f(x) = f(y). Plain birthday search; no differential or structural property of the 5 rounds is used.

Machine, a declared convention of this entry (H3, supporting): a classical load/store machine with 256-bit words, 256-bit immediates and 1856 registers under collision-frontier-v5 (the profile fixes the word size and charges loads and stores, not a register count); 1054 operations (C of blake3-r5) to the unit. Charged: every add, AND, OR, XOR, shift, compare, branch, register move, load, store and the random word. The main loop evaluates 256 trails bit-sliced with pivot full adders: 37255 operations per batch (a rolled step of 37,218 operations: rounds 1-2 straight, rounds 3-5 as 3 iterations of one generic round, with 576 register moves of the message permutation after each of 2 iterations, 12 loop-control operations, no zero-message folding in the loop; a 34-operation stage-1 test, 3 loop operations); it needs 1827 registers. Every instruction is charged 36 bytes, loop control included. Smaller register files are not priced.

time_log2 is an upper bound: every term of proof.md Section 3.4 is enforced by a halt of the program (B batches, e2max stage-1 hits, 17674 table keys, 1 cut trail, a recovery of two passes of at most c + 2^48 batches each, one recovery), and the bound charges each at its limit. The attempt is single: one fresh uniform 256-bit word r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, no advice; m0..m7 = 0. Distinguished points: low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 254 (density 254 / 2^122). The generator that builds the circuit at setup is charged (18,871,000 operations).

Memory: 17674 table entries of 10 bytes (176740 bytes) plus 795996 bytes of code (22111 instructions of 36 bytes, the rolled step 19803 of them) plus 16,384 bytes of counters and the plane copy plus 59,392 bytes for the 1856 registers: 1048512 bytes = 2^19.99991; claimed as 20, the log2 of the 2^20-byte budget (the scalar policy adds 0 to time_log2). The circuit generator that runs at setup is a two-pass C program charged at 2249 compiled instructions (80964 bytes) and 34716 bytes of scratch, held in the region that the table and the register file occupy once the search runs: setup phase 928060 bytes, search phase 1048512 (proof 3.6). It was run in a sandbox capped at 1,048,576 bytes of guest memory and as a native binary with its address space capped at 2^20 bytes; both emit the identical program.

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 of proof.md Section 4 proves it for a uniformly random function from the lazy-sampling hazard (a supermartingale over the evaluations, no conditioning on which trails finish, the cut count bounded by a proved theorem; bound 0.39000, exact certificate in Appendix A, none spare); H1, score-critical (clauses (a) to (d), declared and not proved), says the real attempt succeeds at least as often. Nothing else in the bound is heuristic. If the hazard were (1 - eps) / N the plan needs extra time: 0.0072 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.

The declared experiments run this program in the organizer sandbox: bsrho-n18 (one attempt of the 256-lane search per trial at width 18, DP = low 2 bits zero) and proj-k0-w256 (2048 points of the target at width 256 per trial, a pair when two digests agree in the low 21 bits). Each returns pairs whose complete 5-round digests agree in the stated low bits. They are program checks: no number of the claim is estimated from their counts and no sampling premise is used. No outside code or library is used.

No nonuniform advice and no prefix: q = 0 is derived by the generator. Credited derivative: our own 4a9f31b8 (the same search, plan method and proof, with a straight-line five-round step), a2e94df7 (the rolled step, generator, ledger and proof at 7 rounds), a6ee439c (the same program and proof at 4 rounds), 41b32afc, 75d5e1f9, 62cfd777 (3 rounds), 0a9640ed and 3356413f (program, search, ledger, register convention), and jungjipdo's 6ae36351 for the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q (re-implemented from its proof text; no file of it used or run). preprocessing_log2 = 14.2 is the setup and generator row, which is also inside time_log2.

heuristics.statement: Model premise, four clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds, with the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q (f(x) = the complete 5-round digest of the 64-byte message 0^32 || x, q = 0 the digest-plane mask of the generated program), is at least the probability P_F, over the fresh word r and a uniformly random F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation of g is replaced by F (lazy sampling). Clauses: (a) distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256, uniform and independent outputs; (b) the iterates from r + t have the first-collision law of a random mapping; (c) a point is a distinguished point (low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 254) with probability 254 / 2^122, independently of the collision events; (d) adaptivity: the program chooses its points, and which trails finish, are cut or abort, from earlier outputs of g; given the whole history of the run and which later outputs are distinguished points, a fresh evaluation equals a given earlier non-distinguished output with probability at least 2^-256 (the lazy-sampling hazard of F). Proof.md Section 4 (Lemma 2) proves P_F >= 0.3900 for F from the hazard alone, by a supermartingale over the evaluations, with no conditioning on which trails finish and no fixed-size birthday step; (d) is the premise that g has that hazard. This is a comparison of two success events, not a statement about the entropy of r. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r5-prefix-v1 restricted to 64-byte messages 0^32 || x, the fixed mask q, the 2^128-scale evaluation of g along about 16700 trails of mean length 2^114.01 started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved: an assumption, no proof is known. The full 256-bit functional graph, trails longer than 2^40 and 2^128 evaluations cannot be observed. The organizer experiments bsrho-n18 and proj-k0-w256 run this program on the real target at reduced width (the search at width 18) and at full width for 2048 points with 21-bit projections; they are program checks, no number of the claim is estimated from their counts, and no sampling premise is used. Extrapolation from these sizes to width 256 and 2^128 evaluations is by the premise only. If the collision hazard is (1 - eps) / N instead of 1 / N (clause (d), or a deficit eps in clause (a)), the plan of this program needs, to restore 0.39: 0.0072 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about one fixed function, not a theorem: on the target the run is a deterministic function of r. It cannot be tested at width 256; the experiments reach width 18 and 21-bit projections of 2048 points per trial and do not measure collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. The bound has no margin above 0.39 (B is the least multiple of 10^24 that reaches it), so any hazard deficit is repaired by extra time, priced above: 0.0072 bit for eps = 0.01 (Tp 253); 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05 (Tp 247); 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10 (Tp 241); 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25 (Tp 220).

heuristics.statement: Declared machine convention of this entry (supporting; a convention, not a claim about the benchmark; the register-file convention of our 0a9640ed and a2e94df7, here with 1856 registers). The cost model prices a 256-bit word RAM with loads and stores and fixes no register count; this entry declares R = 1856 registers of 256 bits, counted as 59,392 bytes of memory, and charges every operation, load, store and register move. The main loop (one batch of 256 trails, 37255 operations: the 37,218-operation generated step, a 34-operation stage-1 test and 3 loop operations) has no load or store; it has the register moves of the message permutation (576 plane copies after each of the first two iterations of the round loop), the setup of the message slots (512 operations), the complements (240) and the loop control (12 operations), all counted. The generated program uses 1827 registers; the rest are for the loop counters and handlers. The organizer's reference count C(r5) = 1054 is used only as the unit. Every instruction is charged 36 bytes of code, also the three-register ones and the loop-control ones (no decode is free), and the code of the circuit generator is charged at 36 bytes per instruction of its compiled form (2249 instructions, proof.md 3.6).
heuristics.scope: The loop body of one batch of 256 lanes, its stage-1 test and the handlers; table accesses, recovery, events and setup are charged at the stated bounds including loads and stores of their words.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine with fewer than 1827 registers would add loads and stores to the loop body; that cost is not priced for the rolled program (proof.md 3.5) and not claimed. The claim assumes the declared 1856.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile does not fix a register count or an instruction set; the declaration is this entry's own, as is the reading of the loop (counted loop-control operations and instructions, register moves for the message permutation, no free decode or re-indexing). The counts (37,218 operations, 19,803 instructions, 1827 registers) are produced by the generator in the program (a C port emits the identical program in a memory-capped sandbox, proof 3.6); smaller register files are not priced.
